question: For the thermosetting resin found to decompose most easily in molten alkali hydroxide, how much CH4 (mg/g) was produced in KOH at 500 °C?
rendered:
Document: "Dissolution and gasification behavior of thermosetting resin in molten alkali hydroxide"

The document states that epoxy resin decomposed most easily in molten alkali hydroxide, and the gas composition (H2, CH4, CO, and CO2) from epoxy resin treated with KOH at various temperatures is summarized in Table 1.

Table 1:

| Temperature (°C) | H2 | CH4 | CO | CO2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 150 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 200 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 250 | 0.1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 300 | 15.2 | 0.8 | 16.0 | 0 |
| 350 | 25.5 | 1.3 | 21.7 | 0 |
| 400 | 98.8 | 39.6 | 194.8 | 0 |
| 500 | 114.2 | 0.6 | 222.0 | 0 |

At 500 °C, the amount of CH4 produced from epoxy resin treated with KOH is 0.6 mg/g.

Answer: 0.6 mg/g.
